title: Crypto market slips as ARC lifts portfolio value
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded around $78,040, down 1% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell 1.5% to roughly $2,458. CoinGabbar's CoinGecko-based market report put total crypto capitalization at $2.76 trillion, down 0.9%, with DeFi dropping 3.8%. The pullback extended beyond the two largest assets, though losses were uneven across sectors. Arbitrum's ARB fell 8.2%, illustrating the sharper losses in parts of the altcoin market.

In macro news, the U.S. Treasury announced a buyback of up to $6 billion in bonds with 10 to 20 years remaining, tripling the $2 billion cap on its previous operation in that maturity range. The purchase is scheduled and has not yet taken place. Treasury classifies it as liquidity support. For crypto, smoother government-bond trading could help the broader funding environment, but the announced purchase ceiling alone does not establish that more money will flow into digital assets.

Consensys plans to separate its consumer and institutional businesses into independently operated companies. The existing company will become MetaMask, led by Joe Lubin, while a new Consensys led by Mike Kriak will house institutional infrastructure and protocol work, including Linea. Completion is expected by year-end. The proposed structure gives the wallet business and enterprise infrastructure separate management and investment priorities. It also makes MetaMask's expansion into everyday financial services a more explicit business focus.

Trezor disclosed a breach at its third-party email provider after customers received phishing messages alleging an STM32 entropy vulnerability. A response on its official forum said the affected domain had been taken down and the incident was under investigation. The practical risk is that an apparently familiar sender can carry a malicious security alert. Customers should disregard the message and avoid entering wallet recovery words into any linked verification tool.

Our two wallets total about $123,705: $111,464 in the Safe and $12,241 in the active treasury. Against the previous verified snapshot, combined marked value rose $3,125, or 2.6%. The Safe gained about $3,351 while the active treasury declined $226. The Safe's 26.74 million ARC balance is unchanged at displayed precision, but its value rose about $3,330 to $93,833. That holding alone represents roughly 76% of the portfolio, with additional ARC exposure in the two WETH/ARC liquidity pools, together worth about $15,067.

Other material positions include $4,436 in cbETH and $1,938 across Beefy vaults. Aave shows about $8,387 of supplied WETH against $2,917 of USDC debt, with health factors of 3.06 in the treasury and 2.04 in the Safe, both lower than before. Fluid is only about $200 net, but carries roughly $1,003 of debt and a 1.08 health factor, leaving little liquidation headroom.
